variants.omim_name: WNT10B, HOMOZYGOUS 4-BP DUPLICATION RESULTING IN A PREMATURE TERMINATION CODON
as_reported: homozygous 4-bp duplication resulting in a premature termination codon
variants.consequence: frameshift duplication with premature termination codon

records.label: Two sibs with split foot
quotes: Another case of split-foot mutation in two sibs.

records.label: Intermarried consanguineous family
records.segregation: Affected in two sibships, each from a first-cousin marriage
quotes: A intermarried consanguineous family with split-hand and -foot deformity occurring in two sibship is presented. Both the sibship resulted from marriage between first cousins.

records.label: Extended family with ectrodactyly in sisters and half sisters
quotes: An extended family is described in which four sisters and half sisters presented with ectrodactyly. Two of the sisters had associated agenesis of the tibiae.
An autosomal recessive gene seems likely to be the mode of inheritance.

records.label: Sisters and half sisters with ectrodactyly
quotes: Ectrodactyly in sisters and half sisters.

records.label: Family with split hand/foot malformation in two sibships
quotes: A family is described in which four subjects in two sibships had typical split hand/foot malformation.

records.label: Inbred kindred with nine SHFM cases
quotes: Here we report on nine cases of SHFM in an inbred kindred. A variable intrafamilial expression of the malformation pattern is apparent.
Autosomal recessive inheritance and a two-locus model are discussed.

records.label: Large consanguineous kindred with autosomal recessive SHFM
records.segregation: WNT10B p.R332W homozygous in 12 affected members but not in the atypical case; also homozygous in one asymptomatic (non-penetrant) female. TP63 insertion variant found in most affected subjects.
quotes: We studied a large consanguineous kindred afflicted with autosomal recessive SHFM. Twelve affected members had central feet reductions with or without hand involvement while the remaining one had the mildest phenotype and atypical SHFM.
a homozygous missense WNT10b mutation (p.R332W) in all affected individuals but the atypical case plus in an asymptomatic female.
we detected in most affected subjects a rare insertion variant (rs34201045) at the alternate promoter used for transcription of the N-terminal-truncated p63 isotype.

records.label: Patient with sporadic SHFM

variants.as_reported: homozygous 4-bp duplication resulting in a premature termination codon
variants.consequence: frameshift duplication with premature termination codon

quotes: By examining WNT10B in a patient with sporadic SHFM, we identified a homozygous 4-bp duplication resulting in a premature termination codon. Nine heterozygous relatives show no sign of SHFM.

records.label: Indian girl with SHFM
quotes: We report an Indian girl with split-hand/foot malformation (SHFM), sparse hair, and interrupted eyebrows, who carries a novel homozygous deletion c.695_697delACA in WNT10B.
The patient and all family members had normal bone density and they were not obese like some of the patients with WNT10B variants.

notes.statement: Kantaputra et al. (2018) used protein modeling to predict that the WNT10B p.Asn232del deletion, at a critical position in the protein structure, was likely to severely affect protein structure and function, likely decreasing protein lifetime and preventing binding to its receptors and other ligands.
quotes: According to the protein model, this single amino acid deletion at the critical position in the protein structure is likely to severely affect the protein structure and function.
This deletion is likely to lead decreased lifetime and make it unable to bind to its receptors and other ligands.

notes.statement: Kantaputra et al. (2018) suggested that sparse hair and interrupted eyebrows may be associated findings of SHFM6.
quotes: Sparse hair and interrupted eyebrows may be associated findings of SHFM6.

notes.statement: Blattner et al. (2010) concluded that sporadic SHFM is not always a dominant trait and may show recessive inheritance, implying a 25% recurrence risk for sibs and a very low recurrence risk for offspring of patients unless there is consanguinity.
quotes: Obviously, sporadic SHFM may show recessive rather than dominant inheritance resulting in a 25% recurrence risk for sibs instead of a very low-recurrence risk as generally presumed.
It can be concluded that sporadic SHFM is not always a dominant trait.

notes.statement: Blattner et al. (2010) recommended that patients with sporadic SHFM be tested for WNT10B mutations to determine the recurrence risk.
quotes: To determine the recurrence risk, patients affected with sporadic SHFM should be tested for mutations in WNT10B.

notes.statement: By homozygosity mapping in a large consanguineous kindred with autosomal recessive SHFM, Ugur and Tolun (2008) identified a novel SHFM locus at 12q13.11-q13, with a maximum multipoint lod score of 5.47.
quotes: We identified by homozygosity mapping a novel SHFM locus at 12q13.11-q13 with a maximum multipoint lod score of 5.47

notes.statement: Ugur and Tolun (2008) excluded linkage to 4 of the 5 known SHFM loci in their kindred; at TP63 (SHFM4), they detected in most affected subjects a rare insertion variant (rs34201045) at the alternate promoter used for transcription of the N-terminally truncated p63 isotype.
quotes: We also investigated linkage to the five known SHFM loci. Four of the loci were excluded, while in TP63 [tumor protein p63 (SHFM4)], the only known gene responsible for SHFM, we detected in most affected subjects a rare insertion variant (rs34201045)

notes.statement: Because an asymptomatic female was homozygous for the WNT10B mutation, Ugur and Tolun (2008) proposed that either a second locus contributes to manifestation of the SHFM phenotype or a suppressor locus prevented trait manifestation in the nonpenetrant female, suggesting complex inheritance.
quotes: We propose that either a second locus contributes to the manifestation of SHFM phenotype or a suppressor locus prevented trait manifestation in the non-penetrant female.

notes.statement: Elliott and Evans (2006) noted that split-hand/foot malformation is genetically heterogeneous, with at least 5 loci identified, and that it occurs both as an isolated malformation and as part of syndromes, with variable expressivity and reduced penetrance.
quotes: This variability causes the phenotypic classification of SHFM to be far from straightforward and genetic heterogeneity, with at least five loci identified to date, further complicates management of affected patients and their families.

notes.statement: Using descriptive epidemiology, chi-square and discriminant function analyses, Elliott and Evans (2006) identified phenotypic patterns associated with the mapped SHFM loci. They suggested that these patterns could help with classification and guide mapping efforts and targeted genetic testing.
quotes: Using descriptive epidemiology, Chi square and discriminant function analyses, our laboratory has identified phenotypic patterns associated with the mapped genetic SHFM loci.
These findings can assist in classification, provide insight into responsible developmental genes and assist in directing mapping efforts and targeted genetic testing

notes.statement: Gül and Oktenli (2002) described nine cases of split hand/split foot malformation in an inbred kindred and discussed autosomal recessive inheritance and a two-locus model, in contrast to the autosomal dominant inheritance seen in most familial cases.
quotes: The majority of the familial cases are inherited in an autosomal dominant manner.
Autosomal recessive inheritance and a two-locus model are discussed.

notes.statement: Freire-Maia (1971) described a recessive form of ectrodactyly and discussed its implications for genetic counseling.
quotes: A recessive form of ectrodactyly, and its implications in genetic counseling.

notes.statement: Mufti and Wood (1987) concluded that autosomal recessive inheritance seemed likely in an extended family in which 4 sisters and half sisters had ectrodactyly.
quotes: An autosomal recessive gene seems likely to be the mode of inheritance.

notes.statement: Zlotogora and Nubani (1989) described a family in which 4 individuals in 2 sibships had typical split hand/foot malformation. They discussed the possibility of a rare autosomal recessive form of the malformation. As another possibility, they proposed a two-locus model: a dominant mutation at a second, controlling locus would cause non-penetrance of the dominant split hand/foot mutation.
quotes: The possibility of the existence of a rare autosomal recessive form of the malformation is discussed, as well as a two locus model.

In the two locus model the dominant mutation leading to the split hand/foot malformation is controlled by a gene at another locus. A dominant mutation at the controlling locus leads to non-penetrance of the split hand/foot mutation.

notes.statement: Verma et al. (1976) concluded that their report, together with those of Ray (1960) and Freire-Maia (1971), further demonstrated that split-hand and -foot deformity can be inherited as an autosomal recessive trait.
quotes: This report, together with those of Ray (1960) and Freire-Maia (1971), further demonstrates that split-hand and -foot deformity can be inherited as an autosomal recessive trait.
